{{Short description|Soviet and Russian mathematician}}
'''Rifkat Ibragimovich Bogdanov''' ({{langx|ru|Рифка́т Ибраги́мович Богда́нов}}; June 13, 1950 &ndash; November 3, 2013) was a [[USSR|Soviet]] and [[Russia]]n [[mathematician]] known for contributions to [[nonlinear dynamical systems]], [[bifurcation theory]], and [[differential geometry]]. He was an ethnic [[Tatars|Tatar]].{{cn|date=September 2026}} In his work on bifurcations of [[limit cycles]] and [[versal deformations]] of [[Mathematical singularity|singular points]] of [[vector fields]] (1975&ndash;76), he described a bifurcation of [[co-dimension]] 2, which has become known in the literature as the [[Bogdanov–Takens bifurcation]].

Born in the village of [[Mamykovo]] in [[Tatarstan]], Bogdanov had a doctorate under the supervision of [[Vladimir Arnold]]<ref>https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=79232</ref> in physico-mathematical sciences and was a professor in two Russian research organizations: the [[Skobeltsyn Institute of Nuclear Physics]] at [[Lomonosov Moscow State University]] and the Department of Higher Mathematics at MATI &mdash; the [[Tsiolkovskii State Technological University]].

== See also ==
* [[Bogdanov–Takens bifurcation]]

== Selected publications ==
* R. I. Bogdanov (1975). "Versal deformation of a singular point of a vector field with zero eigenvalues," ''Functional Analysis and Its Applications'' '''9''': 63 [in Russian].
* R. I. Bogdanov (1976). "Bifurcations of the limit cycle of a family of vector fields on a plane," ''Transactions I. G. Petrovskii Seminar, Moscow State University'' '''2''': 23&ndash;35 [in Russian; English translation in ''Selecta Mathematica Sovietica'' '''1''': 373&ndash;388, 1981].
* R. I. Bogdanov (1979). "Versal deformations of singular points of vector fields on a plane," ''Functional Analysis and Its Applications'' '''13''': 63&ndash;64 [in Russian; English translation available].
* R. I. Bogdanov (2003). ''Nonlinear Dynamical Systems on a Plane and Their Applications'', Vuzovskaya Kniga Publishing House, Moscow [in Russian].
